```{r}
#| label: setup

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (
      file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(candidate, "_quarto.yml"))
    ) {
      return(candidate)
    }
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the project root", call. = FALSE)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

predictor_labels <- c(
  work_free_day = "Free day versus work day",
  activity_status = "Active versus sedentary",
  previous_sleep_duration_centered_h = "Previous sleep duration (per hour)",
  weekday_weekend = "Weekend versus weekday"

display_predictor <- function(x) {
  out <- unname(predictor_labels[x])
  out[is.na(out)] <- x[is.na(out)]
  out
}

format_effect <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 2L) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f × (%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f)"),
    estimate, low, high
  )
}

format_p_cell <- function(value, significant = FALSE) {
  display <- nh_p_value_display(value, significant = significant)
  ifelse(
    display$p_bold,
    paste0("**", display$p_display, "**"),
    display$p_display
  )
}

compact_gt <- function(
  data,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  source_note = NULL,
  groupname_col = NULL
) {
  output <- gt::gt(data, groupname_col = groupname_col) |>
    gt::opt_row_striping() |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.font.size = gt::px(12),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(4),
      heading.align = "left",
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(10)
    )
  if (!is.null(title) || !is.null(subtitle)) {
    output <- gt::tab_header(output, title = title, subtitle = subtitle)
  }
  if (!is.null(source_note)) {
    output <- gt::tab_source_note(output, source_note = source_note)
  }
  output
}
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Stage 2 result gate — author review required"}
This report implements the author-approved H06-002 population-mean contract.
All planned models are numerically estimable, but the diagnostics show
substantial overdispersion, imperfect mean calibration, and residual
within-day and local-clock structure. The activity association is stable
across the declared checks. The work/free association is positive in the
primary analysis but is sensitive to the working variance and to omitting two
sites. The sleep interval includes both a modest decrease and a modest
increase. These are **provisional audit results, not accepted manuscript
claims**. Stage 3 remains blocked until explicit H06-G2 approval.
:::

# Question and controlling contract

The preregistered hypothesis is:

> **H6: Day type, daily exercise, and sleep variables predict daily light exposure metrics.**

DEV-015 records a deliberate adaptation: the registered 15-metric,
participant-day question was judged insufficiently parsimonious and
interpretable, so the selected analysis asks about supported one-hour
zero-aware geometric mean melEDI. This deliberate choice is not treated as an
error. It does change the outcome, analysis unit, weighting of days, temporal
dependence, multiplicity family, and reader-facing wording. The revised
analysis therefore estimates expected hourly melEDI across retained supported
hours; it does not test “daily exposure.”

The primary predictors are work/free day, binary activity status
(sedentary versus any light, moderate, or vigorous reported exercise), and
previous-night sleep duration. Near-eye is primary. Chest, exact paired-day
refits, weekday/weekend, the gap comparison, alternative covariance and
working-variance choices, and targeted deletions have their declared
supporting roles. Local clock is not a confirmatory covariate because the
author requested an average across retained supported hours; exploratory
GAMs separately describe time of day.

## Immutable inputs and identity check

All 15 contract inputs match their approved SHA-256 identities, including the
revised Stage 1 source
`393fd87c908302c1681925dcc451b27be31e652758592da8a81c775ff09aaf26`,
its render
`186ab355deb0ba41f276c55c0490e9e0edbe7be1060c40fe2f4c366ed8eee8ae`,
and decision H06-002
`882057ec11ce5e6a56d5b7268b3b501d372c2ec5a34de21a1ef0fa4ebcf07a52`.
The analytical TUM diary source remains the immutable `melidosData` 1.0.6 pin
(commit `618fda8521f3cf581661ceb2c026e3de7cd9ba82`, DOI
`10.5281/zenodo.16893901`, object SHA-256
`0db56324e9826d427c42984fdfc43eb1e7487211365f222a1c0b2ecff618f1ef`).
The read-only assertion finds **7 TUM S001 rows and 0 S101 rows**, with no
local identifier rewrite. No remote release was fetched and no shared
preparation was rebuilt.

The `KNUST_S005` source numeral 3,600 is interpreted only in the exploratory
H06 adapter as 3,600 seconds = 1 hour. The shared diary is unchanged; this row
does not enter the primary analysis.

# Exact models and inference

The mean is fitted with a zero-inclusive quasi-Poisson log-link GLM.
Participant-cluster HC3 covariance (`fix = FALSE`, finite-cluster correction)
treats participants—not hours—as inferential replicates. One-coefficient
tests use a *t* reference with *G* − 1 degrees of freedom; multi-coefficient
site-interaction tests use Wald *F* with restriction-rank and *G* − 1 degrees
of freedom. Fixed site is sum-coded. Overall ratios are equal-site averages on
the linear-predictor scale followed by one exponential back-transformation.
The covariance permits arbitrary dependence within participant, but it does
not whiten residuals or repair the conditional mean.

```{r}
#| label: exact-confirmatory-formulas
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| code-summary: "Exact evaluated Wilkinson formulas (always shown)"

formula_text <- function(x) paste(deparse(x), collapse = " ")

formula_registry <- tibble::enframe(
  h06_formula_set(), name = "model_id", value = "formula"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(formula = vapply(.data$formula, formula_text, character(1)))

formula_registry |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    role = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$model_id == "additive" ~ "Primary mean and H06-F1/F3",
      .data$model_id == "full" ~ "Site heterogeneity and H06-F2",
      grepl("additive_no", .data$model_id) ~ "Visible hierarchy-preserving reduced model",
      grepl("full_no", .data$model_id) ~ "Visible interaction-block reduced model",
      .data$model_id == "weekend_additive" ~ "Estimate/CI sensitivity only",
      TRUE ~ "Construction reference"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Model = .data$model_id, Role = .data$role,
                `Evaluated Wilkinson formula` = .data$formula) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "All comparisons use identical frozen rows. Quasi-likelihood AIC and ",
      "likelihood-ratio tests are unavailable and are not reported."
    )
  )
```

The active confirmatory multiplicity families each contain exactly three
tests and use Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment. Raw p-values are displayed but
never bolded. Only adjusted p-values at α = 0.050 are bolded. Chest,
paired-placement, covariance, standardization, weekday/weekend, influence,
and exploratory outputs do not create post hoc significance families.

# Exact fitted samples and category cells

The primary near-eye fit contains 16,596 supported hours from 715
participant-days, 137 participants, and all nine sites. Days contribute 19–24
supported hours, so the approved estimand is explicitly supported-hour
weighted. Chest has 18,352 hours, 789 participant-days, 149 participants, and
eight sites.


# Primary near-eye results

```{r}
#| label: primary-effects
#| tbl-cap: "Primary equal-site ratios of expected supported-hour melEDI."

primary_results |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$Predictor, .data$`Ratio (95% CI)`,
    .data$`Raw p`, .data$`BH-adjusted p`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "Quasi-Poisson log mean; sum-coded fixed site; participant-cluster HC3; ",
      "G = 137 and denominator df = 136. Ratios above 1 indicate higher ",
      "expected hourly melEDI. Only adjusted p-values meeting alpha = 0.050 ",
      "are bold."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Raw p`, `BH-adjusted p`))
```

In the primary analysis, expected supported-hour melEDI was 1.45 times as
high on free days as on work days (95% CI 1.14–1.85; BH-adjusted p = 0.004)
and 2.06 times as high on active as on sedentary days (1.54–2.76;
BH-adjusted p < 0.001). The previous-sleep ratio was 0.98 per additional hour
(0.85–1.12; BH-adjusted p = 0.745). The sleep interval is compatible with a
modest decrease or increase; it is not evidence for “no effect.”

```{r}
#| label: primary-site-heterogeneity
#| tbl-cap: "Primary site-interaction block tests."

primary_heterogeneity |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$Predictor, .data$Test, .data$`Raw p`, .data$`BH-adjusted p`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "H06-F2 contains the three declared site-interaction blocks. Only the ",
      "BH-adjusted p-value is eligible for bolding."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Raw p`, `BH-adjusted p`))
```

The work/free association varied across sites (BH-adjusted p = 0.017).
Activity and sleep showed no multiplicity-retained site heterogeneity. The
overall work/free ratio must therefore be presented with its site-specific
variation rather than as a universal site-invariant contrast.

# Required data sensitivity

At first use, this report calls the comparison input the **gap-timing-unaware
dataset**. It still passed the 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules, but
the timing of remaining within-hour and within-day gaps was not used for an
additional metric-specific adjustment. The primary analysis could therefore
be interpreted as time-sensitive. After this one-time qualification, the
current corrected input is called simply the **primary dataset**.

The all-available near-eye comparison has 16,329 hours, 702 participant-days,
137 participants, and nine sites. On the exact common-hour frame, the primary
dataset drops 267 hours and the gap comparison drops none; 16,329 hour keys
remain. Predictors are identical. Only 12 response values differ, so this is
both a sample-composition and a response-construction check rather than a
claim that the two inputs are identical.

```{r}
#| label: gap-exact-common-samples
#| tbl-cap: "Exact common-hour sample for the required data sensitivity."

gap_common_samples |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Placement = dplyr::recode(
      .data$placement, glasses = "Near-eye", chest = "Chest"
    ),
    `Primary hours` = .data$primary_all_hours,
    `Gap-comparison hours` = .data$gap_timing_unaware_all_hours,
    `Exact common hours` = .data$exact_common_hours,
    `Primary-only hours` = .data$primary_only_hours,
    `Gap-only hours` = .data$gap_timing_unaware_only_hours,
    `Common days` = .data$exact_common_participant_days,
    Participants = .data$exact_common_participants,
    Sites = .data$exact_common_sites
  ) |>
  compact_gt() |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric))
```

```{r}
#| label: gap-effect-comparisons
#| tbl-cap: "Primary-versus-gap sensitivity on all available and exact common hours."

sensitivity |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$comparison_id %in% c(
      "primary_vs_gap_timing_unaware_all_available",
      "primary_vs_gap_timing_unaware_exact_common_hours"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Frame = dplyr::recode(
      .data$comparison_id,
      primary_vs_gap_timing_unaware_all_available = "All available",
      primary_vs_gap_timing_unaware_exact_common_hours = "Exact common hours"
    ),
    Predictor = display_predictor(.data$predictor_id),
    Primary = format_effect(
      .data$reference_ratio, .data$reference_conf_low,
      .data$reference_conf_high
    ),
    Gap = format_effect(
      .data$alternative_ratio, .data$alternative_conf_low,
      .data$alternative_conf_high
    ),
    `Primary adjusted p` = format_p_cell(
      .data$reference_p_adjusted, .data$reference_p_adjusted <= 0.05
    ),
    `Gap adjusted p` = format_p_cell(
      .data$alternative_p_adjusted, .data$alternative_p_adjusted <= 0.05
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$Frame, .data$Predictor, .data$Primary, .data$Gap,
    .data$`Primary adjusted p`, .data$`Gap adjusted p`
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    groupname_col = "Frame",
    source_note = paste0(
      "Each input retains its declared three-test BH family. Exact-common ",
      "primary and gap models use identical hour keys."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Primary adjusted p`, `Gap adjusted p`))
```

All three estimates and multiplicity conclusions are stable. The gap
near-eye ratios are 1.44 for free/work, 2.08 for active/sedentary, and 0.96
per hour of sleep. Work/free site heterogeneity also remains
multiplicity-retained (BH-adjusted p = 0.015).

# Diagnostics and limitations

All 12 approved additive/full fits converge; every fixed-effect design is full
rank; and every unmodified HC3 matrix is finite and positive definite. The
48 HC0–HC3 covariance checks are also finite and positive definite. The
largest condition number is 6,998. These results clear the numerical gate,
not the scientific adequacy gate.

```{r}
#| label: core-diagnostic-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Interpreted diagnostics for the six additive mean models."

diagnostic_summary |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Scenario = dplyr::recode(
      .data$run_id,
      main__glasses__all_available = "Primary near-eye",
      main__chest__all_available = "Chest, all available",
      main__glasses__paired_common = "Near-eye, paired days",
      main__chest__paired_common = "Chest, paired days",
      gap_timing_unaware__glasses__all_available = "Gap sensitivity, near-eye",
      gap_timing_unaware__chest__all_available = "Gap sensitivity, chest"
    ),
    `Zero hours` = .data$exact_zero_fraction,
    Dispersion = .data$dispersion,
    `Observed/fitted decile range` = sprintf(
      "%.2f–%.2f", .data$calibration_low, .data$calibration_high
    ),
    `Residual–fitted Spearman` = .data$residual_fitted_spearman,
    `|Residual|–fitted Spearman` =
      .data$absolute_residual_fitted_spearman,
    `Residual lag 1` = .data$lag_1,
    `Residual lag 6` = .data$lag_6,
    Gate = .data$numerical_gate_pass
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "Calibration is in-sample and descriptive, not predictive validation. ",
      "Dispersion is the Pearson working-dispersion estimate."
    )
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = `Zero hours`, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = c(
      Dispersion, `Residual–fitted Spearman`,
      `|Residual|–fitted Spearman`, `Residual lag 1`, `Residual lag 6`
    ),
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::fmt(columns = Gate, fns = function(x) ifelse(x, "PASS", "FAIL"))
```

The primary response contains 28.3% exact-zero hours and the working
dispersion is 3,618. Primary fitted-decile observed/fitted ratios range from
0.78 to 1.61. Residual–fitted Spearman correlation is −0.564 and absolute
residual–fitted correlation is 0.553. These patterns indicate substantial
mean–variance and mean-calibration limitations despite cluster-robust
uncertainty.

Residual correlation remains 0.464 at lag 1 and 0.233 at lag 2 in the primary
near-eye analysis; it approaches 0.013 by lag 6. Chest lag 1 is 0.366.
Participant clustering permits this within-participant dependence for the
covariance estimator, but does not claim that the hourly trajectory has been
modeled. The residual-clock plot shows additional daytime structure. Because
the approved estimand intentionally averages over observed supported hours,
the confirmatory model does not add a post hoc clock term; this limitation is
reported next to the estimate and the exploratory GAM supplies temporal
context.

```{r}

#| fig-alt: "Residual diagnostic plot across local clock hour for the primary near-eye model. Mean residuals vary over the day and a residual-versus-fitted panel shows imperfect mean calibration and increasing spread."
#| fig-cap: "Primary residual structure by local clock and fitted value. Participant-cluster HC3 does not remove these patterns."
#| out-width: 170mm

knitr::include_graphics(artifact(
  "10_figures", "H06", "H06_primary_residual_clock.png"
))
```

## Targeted influence checks

Seven score-ranked participants and all nine sites were deleted one at a time;
all 16 refit sets converged with full-rank designs and positive-definite HC3
covariances. No participant or site was removed from the primary analysis.

```{r}
#| label: influence-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Targeted participant and site deletion results."

influence_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Type = dplyr::recode(
      .data$deletion_type,
      participant = "Participant deletion",
      site = "Site deletion"
    ),
    Predictor = display_predictor(.data$predictor_id),
    `CIs excluding 1` = paste0(.data$`CIs excluding 1`, "/", .data$Deletions)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$Type, .data$Predictor,
    .data$`Largest shift (HC3 SE)`, .data$`CIs excluding 1`
  ) |>
  compact_gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = `Largest shift (HC3 SE)`, decimals = 3)
```

Activity excludes 1 in all 16 deletion checks; sleep excludes 1 in none.
Work/free excludes 1 after every targeted participant deletion but after only
7 of 9 site deletions. Omitting Dortmund gives 1.26 (95% CI 0.98–1.62), and
omitting Borås gives 1.34 (0.99–1.80). TUM S001 and the exploratory
KNUST S005 row are not influential enough to explain the primary result.

## Working-variance, covariance, standardization, and day-type checks

The fixed-power quasi-Tweedie sensitivity (`p = 1.8`) materially changes the
work/free conclusion: 1.15 (95% CI 0.91–1.45; BH-adjusted p = 0.260). Activity
remains 1.91 (1.49–2.45; BH-adjusted p < 0.001), and sleep is 0.95
(0.88–1.04; BH-adjusted p = 0.260). Work/free heterogeneity remains
multiplicity-retained (BH-adjusted p = 0.025). This is why the work/free
result is classified as working-variance sensitive rather than robust.

HC1 and HC2 change uncertainty slightly but not the estimates or qualitative
conclusions. Equal-site and observed-sample standardization coincide for the
additive model. The weekday/weekend substitution gives a weekend/weekday
ratio of 1.23 (95% CI 0.92–1.66); by contract it has an estimate and interval
but no new p-value or multiplicity family.

```{r}
sensitivity |>

      "HC3_vs_HC2",

      HC3_vs_HC1 = "HC3 vs HC1",
      HC3_vs_HC2 = "HC3 vs HC2",
      equal_site_vs_observed_sample = "Equal-site vs observed sample"
    ),
    Predictor = display_predictor(.data$predictor_id),
    Reference = format_effect(
      .data$reference_ratio, .data$reference_conf_low,
      .data$reference_conf_high
    ),
    Alternative = format_effect(
      .data$alternative_ratio, .data$alternative_conf_low,
```

# V0 reconstruction and comparison

V0 deliberately fitted repeated hourly geometric mean melEDI with the fixed
scaffold
`geo.MEDI ~ site * daytype + site * exercise + site * sleep_duration + (1 | Id)`.
The current immutable-pin reconstruction uses 16,500 near-eye and 18,218 chest
hours. **Neither reconstructed V0 model is singular**: both converge, have
positive-definite Hessians, and pass the stored singularity check. V0 is thus
a mathematically valid candidate scaffold, not a failed fit.

It is not an adequate final H06 basis without revision. It uses four-level
exercise rather than the approved binary activity contrast, repeats day-level
predictors over hours without participant-day or residual temporal handling,
uses model-based mixed-model uncertainty rather than the approved participant
cluster inference, and does not implement the current hierarchy,
multiplicity, site-standardization, or reporting contract. Its deliberate
hourly intent is retained; the separable downstream errors are repaired.

The reconstructed near-eye free/work ratio is 0.94 (95% CI 0.85–1.02) and the
sleep ratio is 0.93 per hour (0.90–0.96); chest values are 0.94 (0.86–1.03)
and 0.92 (0.89–0.96). These differ from the revised population-mean results
because the fitted rows, activity definition, dependence/uncertainty
architecture, and estimand implementation differ. The frozen V0 table
reported 0.92 for both free/work and sleep but did not retain 95% intervals.

Revised work-free ratios point above one, unlike V0; revised sleep intervals cross one."
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "V0 and revised H06 estimates. Frozen V0 intervals cannot be recovered from the submitted table. Exercise is excluded because V0's four levels do not match the approved binary activity contrast."
```

## Exploratory time-of-day GAMs

The time-of-day analysis is a separate two-part model: a binomial-logit
occurrence component for melEDI > 0 and a Gamma-log component for positive
melEDI. Within each submitted site and work/free × activity combination, their
product describes expected hourly melEDI. The day-type display averages those
response-scale expected means with equal weight over sedentary and active
status and over all nine sites. The activity display instead averages with
equal weight over work and free days and over all nine sites. Both components
use four cyclic factor-by clock smooths for work/free day × sedentary/active
status, with one shared smoothing parameter (`id = 1`). The parametric
work/free × activity interaction preserves hierarchy. Site enters only as a
parametric fixed adjustment; there is no site-specific clock smooth and no
`sz` component. Participant and participant-day random-effect smooths,
true-sequence `AR.start`, and a working residual correlation remain. The
selected basis is `k = 16`; all fits use
`mgcv::bam(method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE)`. No H06 computation requires
`discrete = FALSE`.

```{r}
#| label: exploratory-two-part-formulas
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| code-summary: "Exploratory two-part formulas (always shown)"

two_part_formula_registry |>
  dplyr::select(
    Component = .data$component,
    Family = .data$response_family,
    `Evaluated Wilkinson formula` = .data$selected_formula,
    Method = .data$method,
    Discrete = .data$discrete,
    `Basis k` = .data$selected_basis_k
  ) |>
  compact_gt(
    source_note = paste0(
      "Exploratory only. Positive-magnitude sequences are rebuilt after ",
      "removing zero hours, so residual correlation never bridges a removed zero."
    )
  )
```

The selected occurrence and positive-magnitude models converge with full-rank
fixed-smooth designs. Working residual correlations are 0.418 and 0.440.
Cyclic closure differences are at most 1.1 × 10^-16 for occurrence and
1.8 × 10^-15 for the combined expected mean. At `k = 16`, the four occurrence
smooths use edf 7.95–9.80 of 14 available and have `k`-check p-values
0.013–0.023. Because edf remains well below the basis ceiling, this is retained
as a residual/model-structure warning rather than interpreted as proof that a
larger basis is required. Positive-magnitude `k`-check p-values are 0.18–0.21.

The occurrence model overpredicts the lowest fitted-probability decile
(observed/fitted ratio 0.829). Positive-magnitude calibration spans roughly
0.89–1.21 and remains weakest in the positive tail. Changing from `k = 12` to
`k = 16` produces a 95th-percentile relative difference of 15.1% for the
combined expected curves. The curves therefore contextualize when exposure
differs; they are not stable confirmatory whole-curve tests and receive no
pointwise significance highlighting.

The work-day curve is solid blue and the free-day curve is dashed orange, with pointwise uncertainty ribbons; curves are averaged equally over sedentary and active status and across nine sites."
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Exploratory expected melEDI by day type across local clock time, standardized with equal weight to sedentary and active status and to each of the nine submitted sites. Curves exclude participant and participant-day random effects; ribbons are approximate pointwise 95% intervals with smoothing parameters fixed and occurrence–magnitude cross-component covariance set to zero. These curves contextualize time of day and are separate from preregistered inference."
```

# Figure readability and reproducibility

All seven reader-facing figures were assessed at 170 mm on an A4 portrait page
with 20-mm side margins. Native and intended widths are equal, so the scale
factor is 1. The five confirmatory/contextual figures retain 8-pt essential
text; the two exploratory figures also retain 8 pt. Physical-size inspection
found no clipping, overlap, harmful wrapping, distortion, or materially
imbalanced data region.

The analysis was run with R 4.6.1. Scientific transformations, checks,
summaries, and models are implemented in H06-scoped R scripts. No package was
installed, no shared data were edited, no heavy resampling was run, and no
full-project render was used. The production command was:

```text
Rscript --vanilla -e '.libPaths(c(normalizePath("renv/library/macos/R-4.6/aarch64-apple-darwin23"), .libPaths())); Sys.setenv(H06_STAGE="fit", H06_REUSE_FITS="true"); sys.source("scripts/hypotheses/H06/run_h06_stage2.R", envir=globalenv())'
```

# H06-G2 decisions requested

The recommended gate disposition is **approve Stage 2 with explicit
qualifications**, not accept every provisional association as equally robust.
Please decide whether to approve the following contract for Stage 3:

1. Accept the quasi-Poisson population-mean model with participant-cluster HC3
   as the H06 primary implementation of the selected supported-hour estimand.
2. Accept the active-versus-sedentary association as stable across the
   declared dataset, placement, covariance, working-variance, and deletion
   checks, while retaining the observational interpretation.
3. Retain the free-versus-work association only with its working-variance,
   site-heterogeneity, and leave-site-out qualifications; do not call it a
   generally robust site-invariant association.
4. Report the previous-sleep result as inconclusive over the interval
   0.85–1.12 per additional hour, not as evidence of no association.
5. Retain chest, paired-day, gap, weekday/weekend, additional-diary, and
   two-part GAM results only in their prespecified contextual, sensitivity, or
   exploratory roles.
6. Accept the documented mean-calibration, residual temporal, and
   local-clock limitations next to the results. No resampling is required for
   H06 Stage 2.

Until the author explicitly approves H06-G2, no result in this report is an
accepted manuscript claim, `notebooks/hypotheses/H06.qmd` must not be created,
and Stage 4 remains blocked.
